run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-100a had issues on November 21, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Between about 13:49 and 14:44 UTC on 2026-11-21, the app-100a payment-api workload (pod label payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-tbgc6, service/job payment-api) logged recurring database connection-pool exhaustion and failing health checks. Log evidence: 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20, active_connections 20 and 27–46 waiting requests whose waits reached 5.2–26.8 s from 2026-11-21T13:49:24Z to 14:43:57Z; 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' (error_code DB_CONN_001, stack at PaymentService.processPayment()/DatabasePool.acquire()); and 'Health check failed - database unreachable', endpoint /healthz, status_code 503, response_time_ms 5009/9684/6354 at 13:57:29Z, 14:01:50Z and 14:44:44Z. The pod's own DB query durations rose from 15–88 ms before 13:45Z to 1252–3106 ms during the issue, then returned to 20–77 ms after 15:01Z, with a successful payment logged again at 14:48:12Z. The observed failure is pool saturation on payment-api driven by a slow or unreachable database dependency; the database itself is not present in any visible namespace, so its identity and why it slowed remain unknown (hypothesis, not fact). No Kubernetes events or object state from the incident hour are available (events in the window only start 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z), and Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for the whole run, so error-rate, restart and caller-impact checks could not be made. No Kubernetes object can be named as the origin, so root_cause is null.

claims.text: The affected workload is Deployment payment-api-100a in namespace app-100a: 1 replica, rollingUpdate maxSurge/maxUnavailable 25%, container 'payment-api' running image python:3.9-slim with command [python /app/app-direct-push.py], container port 8080, livenessProbe httpGet /healthz (initialDelaySeconds 30, periodSeconds 10, timeoutSeconds 10, failureThreshold 3), resources requests 10m/128Mi and limits 256Mi, /app mounted from Secret payment-api-100a-script.

Loki lines for namespace app-100a with labels job=payment-api, service=payment-api, pod_name=payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-tbgc6 record 'ERROR Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20, active_connections 20 and waiting_requests between 27 and 46, wait_time_ms between 5216 and 26789; the earliest returned such line is at 2026-11-21T13:49:24Z and the latest at 2026-11-21T14:43:57Z. The same stream contains 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' with error_code DB_CONN_001 and stack_trace 'at PaymentService.processPayment() / at DatabasePool.acquire()' (e.g. 13:50:55Z, 14:08:14Z, 14:18:41Z, 14:43:09Z, 14:43:57Z).
payment-api's own /healthz checks failed with 'Health check failed - database unreachable', status_code 503 and response_time_ms 5009 at 2026-11-21T13:57:29Z, 9684 at 14:01:50Z and 6354 at 14:44:44Z.

Database query durations logged by payment-api (message 'Database query executed') were 15 ms at 13:06:28Z, 18 ms at 13:17:12Z, 88 ms at 13:17-13:20Z and 65 ms at 13:34:45Z before the incident; 1252 ms at 13:50:55Z, 2355 ms at 14:43:57Z and 3106 ms at 14:28:27Z during it; and 20, 40, 41, 54, 77 ms between 15:01:00Z and 15:15:23Z afterwards.

A 5-minute count_over_time series by level for app-100a logs shows ERROR at zero from 12:05Z until the point ending 13:50Z, first non-zero in the interval ending 13:50Z, non-zero through roughly 14:49Z and not present in later intervals up to 16:59Z, while INFO and DEBUG lines continue throughout the same span.

In the returned log lines the last 'Payment processed successfully' before the error burst is at 2026-11-21T13:31:51Z (processing_time_ms 468) and the next is at 14:48:12Z (processing_time_ms 183), after the last 'database unreachable' line at 14:44:44Z; further successes follow at 14:55:37Z, 15:00:05Z, 15:08:29Z, 15:11:53Z and 15:15:23Z.

No database workload is visible in the cluster: namespaces are app-100a, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; the only StatefulSet is otel-demo/alertmanager (image quay.io/prometheus/alertmanager:v0.28.1); the pods are kube-system components plus otel-demo services (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, load-generator, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping), valkey-cart, jaeger, prometheus, alertmanager, flagd, kube-state-metrics; and the only Service in app-100a is 'loki' (ClusterIP, port 3100).

The payment-api-100a Deployment currently reports 1 replica available and ready (conditions MinimumReplicasAvailable and NewReplicaSetAvailable, observedGeneration 1) with ReplicaSet payment-api-100a-64dcc58445 created 2026-11-22T10:38:38Z and 1/1 ready replicas; this is state at the time of the query (2026-11-22T10:39-10:40Z), after the incident window, not at 2026-11-21 13:45Z.

The only Kubernetes events inside the authorized window span 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z-10:38:39Z: Normal Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started for pods loki-66445c6d6f-nqq2p and payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-tbgc6, SuccessfulCreate for their ReplicaSets and ScalingReplicaSet for loki and payment-api-100a; the single Warning is Endpoints app-219/mariadb 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-219/mariadb: endpoints "mariadb" already exists' at 10:07:47Z, a different namespace roughly 20 hours after the payment-api incident.

The 2026-11-21 Loki records for app-100a carry job=payment-api, service=payment-api, namespace=app-100a and pod_name=payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-tbgc6, and the pod template runs /app/app-direct-push.py, i.e. the application pushes these records itself rather than their being scraped from the container's own stdout history.

In the otel-demo flagd ConfigMap (namespace otel-demo, not app-100a) the fault flags paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable') both declare defaultVariant "off" and state ENABLED; this is the ConfigMap's state when queried on 2026-11-22, not at incident time.

The proximate cause of payment-api's failure is its database dependency: the pod's own DB query durations jumped from 15-88 ms before 13:45Z to 1252-3106 ms, '/healthz' reported 'database unreachable' with 5-9.7 s response times, and the fixed pool of 20 connections stayed fully occupied (active_connections 20) with 27-46 waiting requests between 13:49Z and 14:44Z, producing DB_CONN_001 and 503 health responses. The database itself is not observable here, so this is inferred from payment-api's client-side evidence.

An alternative candidate not excluded for the same pool exhaustion is a surge of concurrent payment traffic against the fixed pool_size 20 (waiting_requests reached 46 at 14:30:57Z) rather than database slowness; no request-rate or database-side metric was available to separate the two, so neither can be confirmed or dismissed from logs alone.

The otel-demo flagd fault flags paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are not supported as the cause of the app-100a payment-api incident: the queried definitions default to "off", the ConfigMap lives in namespace otel-demo and governs the otel-demo 'payment' service, and no evidence ties it to the app-100a payment-api workload or to 2026-11-21 13:45Z (its state at that time is unknown).

The returned event set contains no OOMKilled, Evicted, BackOff, Unhealthy, Failed or restart-type event for payment-api-100a, and the Deployment currently reports 1/1 ready replicas with no restart recorded in the current objects; however these were read on 2026-11-22 and the event set only begins 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z, so they neither confirm nor clear the pod's state at 2026-11-21 13:45Z.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for this run: get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so ERROR-rate, latency, kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and other metric series could not be checked; their absence is unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services and traces_search for service 'payment' in 13:30-14:00Z both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so caller/upstream impact of the payment-api 503s is unverified and no parent-child call edges can be asserted.

The database that payment-api connects to could not be identified: no database pod, StatefulSet or Service exists in any of the eight namespaces (app-100a contains only Service 'loki'), so that dependency's health, latency, restarts and saturation at 13:45Z are unknown.

Deployment payment-api-100a runs /app/app-direct-push.py from Secret payment-api-100a-script; secrets cannot be read, so the database endpoint, pool size, timeouts and any fault-injection setting inside that script could not be verified.

No Kubernetes events exist for 2026-11-21 13:45Z: the returned event set spans only 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z-10:38:39Z, so pod restarts, probe failures or evictions at incident time are unknown (events expire).

The fetch_pod_logs query for pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-tbgc6 returned status no_data with zero lines (previous container not found), so current container stdout could not corroborate the Loki records.
The 2026-11-21 Loki records carry the same pod_name as the pod created 2026-11-22T10:38:39Z; which pod instance emitted them at incident time could not be established.
The NetworkPolicy query returned status no_data with no objects, so ingress/egress policy state around the incident is unchecked rather than proven absent.
The change_history integration is not available, so no deployment or configuration change can be attributed around 2026-11-21 13:45Z.
next_steps: Identify payment-api's database from the Secret payment-api-100a-script or app configuration, then examine that database's latency, connection counts and availability around 2026-11-21T13:45-14:45Z.

Once Prometheus is reachable, check payment-api error ratio, request rate, DB latency and kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total for 2026-11-21 13:00-15:30Z to confirm onset, recovery and any restarts.
Once Jaeger is reachable, inspect spans of payment-api's callers in the same window to determine whether the 503s propagated upstream.
Review the fixed pool_size 20 and acquire timeout against the observed waiting_requests up to 46 and waits up to 26.8 s as a capacity recommendation.
Add alerting on pool saturation and on /healthz 503 'database unreachable' for payment-api, since the incident was visible only in application logs.
